summary.headline: Kiaasa Retail FY26 revenue of ₹134.63 crore, EBITDA margin 17.8% and PAT ₹11.17 crore (+24% YoY); plan of 250 EBOs by 2028.
summary.overview: Kiaasa Retail, a Tier 2/3-focused omni-channel women's ethnic wear brand listed on BSE SME in March 2026, reported FY26 revenue from operations of ₹134.63 crore, EBITDA of ₹24 crore (17.8% margin) and net profit of ₹11.17 crore (+24% YoY). Same-store sales growth accelerated to 12.89%, and the company had 124+ active EBOs across 70+ cities as of May 2026. Management attributed margin expansion to sourcing efficiencies and bulk procurement, and laid out a 250-store target by 2028 and 35% revenue CAGR ambition to FY30. Online contribution remains minimal at about 1-2% of revenue.

financial_highlights.change: Rahul S (Q&A) cited 11.2% growth in FY26; not confirmed by management
Analyst cited ~13-14% prior year, implying ~400-500 bps expansion; not confirmed by management
Up from 7.1% per analyst's reading of presentation

segments.name: Salwar kurta dupatta sets
segments.commentary: Contribute more than half of product mix; average selling price is around ₹2,000 to ₹2,500 and this is the primary revenue and margin engine.

segments.name: Kiaasa Divas (kids, ages 3-13)
segments.commentary: Piloted in 25-26 stores in the last festive season; management expects 8-10% contribution over time.

segments.name: DIY studio
segments.commentary: Bespoke ready-to-stitch format in larger stores; expected 4-5% contribution initially, rising to 10-12% in a couple of years. Store size of 1,200-1,500 sq ft for these formats.

segments.name: Nine99 (factory outlet / clearance)
segments.commentary: Fixed-price stores selling Kiaasa items below ₹999; about 7-10 stores, opened from 2024-25 in smaller towns with one staff member. Revenue contribution not disclosed.

segments.name: MBO / LFS (large format)
segments.commentary: Planned entry in FY27, with a Reliance offer for about 150 counters cited; partner margin of 28-32%. Management said it is a brand-awareness channel with limited PAT impact. Target 600-1,000 counters by 2030.

guidance_outlook: Store network target of 250 EBOs by 2028 (124 operational today); about 66 stores to be opened in next two years funded by IPO proceeds.
Management reiterated long-term vision: revenue CAGR of about 35% and EBITDA CAGR of about 45% through FY30; analyst summary was confirmed as 'yes, almost' with no formal EBITDA target given.
IPO proceeds of about ₹46 crore earmarked for store opening, capex and inventory only.
Future stores to be mainly COCO; FOFO considered once detailed project is planned. Global expansion (Dubai, London, Canada) targeted within 3-5 years, likely 2027-28 planning.
Online revenue expected to grow to about 10-12% of total in the next couple of years.
capex_capacity: Average store capex, inventory and opex data referenced on presentation slide 17 for 700-1,000 sq ft stores; analyst cited ~₹24-25 lakh capex per store, which management said is correct but varies by market, mall and high street.
New stores planned at around 1,500 sq ft for bigger cities, with some 1,200-1,500 sq ft stores for Divas and DIY studio formats.
Store count to rise from 124 to 213 per analyst's reading, with COCO stores from 110 to 198; management framed 250 as the 2028 target.
Fulfilment: online orders served from nearest physical store; same-city delivery within 2 hours (within 4-5 km, via Porter); intercity 2-3 days, maximum 3 days.
demand_pricing: Management says Indian women's ethnic wear market is projected at ₹2.5 lakh crore by 2030 with 7% annual growth.
Same-store sales growth driven by both volume and ASP; management said 10-15% of stock is higher-priced to lift ASP, and ASP has risen while average bill value has stayed flat.
Customer mix: about 70% new customers, 30% repeat; target to raise repeat share to 50% or more.
Sourcing via dedicated contract manufacturers; management said bulk volume orders give better pricing and supplier profiling is used to retain reliable vendors.
Margin improvement attributed to sourcing efficiencies and bulk procurement, plus operating cost control; no quantified split given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 400-500 bps EBITDA margin expansion to 17-18%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited improved sourcing efficiency, better vendor negotiation through bulk procurement and tighter control of operating parts; said cost minimisation will drive better margins over the next five years, without a quantified baseline.

qa_highlights.question: How is the shift to Tier 2/3 cities affecting store-level margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tier 2/3 cities now contribute the most, with consumers willing to pay for affordable luxury; ASP of ₹2,000-2,500 is an aggregate, and the plan is to build footfall first and then raise ASP with new items.

qa_highlights.question: How will the IPO proceeds (about ₹46 crore) be deployed and what revenue will follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Proceeds are for store opening only, covering capex and inventory, to open around 66 stores in the next two years; no revenue figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Store sizes, unit economics and capex for new stores; revenue and EBITDA targets for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Current stores are 700-1,000 sq ft; new stores to be around 1,500 sq ft in bigger cities, with some 1,200-1,500 sq ft formats. No EBITDA target given; referred to slide 20 for the FY30 vision of 35% revenue CAGR and EBITDA growth of roughly 45% CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: What share of same-store growth came from volume versus pricing, and why is ASP up while bill value is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split volume and price. It cited brand awareness, repeat customers and new signature stories for ASP lift, and said store staff up-selling is lagging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MBO/LFS margin profile and working capital cycle, and what is the Nine99 payback?
qa_highlights.answer: MBO margin for partner is 28-32%, so PAT impact is limited but it adds footfall and awareness. Nine99 stores are cheap, low-rent, single-staff units; no payback period or revenue split was given.

qa_highlights.question: How does the FY30 revenue CAGR of 35% reconcile with FY26 growth of 11.2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan includes about 100 more stores beyond 250 by 2030, online growth, and 600-1,000 LFS counters by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Online versus EBO revenue split for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Online is about 1-2% of revenue today and expected to reach about 10-12% over the next couple of years; no split for FY27 was given.

risks_watch: Execution risk on 66 stores in two years and 250 by 2028, with IPO funds covering only part of the plan.
Margin sustainability: EBITDA margin gain is not yet quantified as a baseline; ASP lift has not yet converted into higher average bill value.
Reliance-linked MBO/LFS expansion with 28-32% partner margin and limited PAT contribution.
Vendor concentration with dedicated contract manufacturers; management says pricing is favourable but gave no detail on alternatives.
Global expansion timing (Dubai, London, Canada) is unclear and was described as slow, with planning in FY27-28.
Q&A call quality was poor, with multiple questions repeated or inaudible; the 35% CAGR target and some figures came from analyst readings of slides not verified in the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and ambitious on store expansion and long-term vision, but vague on quantified targets (no EBITDA guidance, no ASP or volume split, no Nine99 economics). Answers were often generic and sometimes deflected to slides.

growth.why: Management targets 250 EBOs by 2028 (124 operating today, ~66 openings over two years funded by ~₹46 crore IPO proceeds) and a ~35% revenue CAGR to FY30, with partial support from the store pipeline, same-store sales growth of 12.89% and new formats; no quarterly revenue or EBITDA growth was confirmed by management.
